# Wardriver wire schema reference

`device_sync.proto`, `observations.proto` and `LICENSE` retain exact upstream
bytes from Blue Swallow Wardriver commit
`2b5a526bac6cf2914c967fa61a185b4ff3db70e8`. Original paths are
`core/model/src/main/proto/` and repository `LICENSE`. These are protocol source,
not a private capture or release artifact.

`node scripts/build-companion-wire.mjs` generates the private
`api/_private/companion/vendor/wire.cjs` using pinned protobufjs 8.8.1 and CLI
2.7.1. Add `--check` to verify reproducibility. The static decoder needs no
runtime code generation or unsafe-eval, and 64-bit integers use Long values.
Full upstream schemas are retained, but the reader admits only its explicitly
supported observation and control protocol. Extra generated types grant no
capability or support claim.

Generated code is excluded from structural/clone metrics by its exact path;
authored reader code remains checked. The protobufjs license is retained beside
the generated module. The browser runtime is bundled from pinned dependencies
when used; no CDN dependency is introduced.

## Producer golden fixture

`tests/fixtures/dataset-wire/producer-golden.json` contains only synthetic
public-key/signed data generated by the actual pinned Kotlin `DatasetWire`
implementation. Its private fixture key is neither exported nor retained.
The generator is `scripts/fixtures/SocietyDatasetGoldenTest.kt`. It deliberately
includes an unknown observation field and a clock above the JavaScript safe
integer limit, a live v2 batch, a closed v1 batch and a signed retraction.

To regenerate in a disposable checkout of the pinned Wardriver commit, copy
the generator into its matching `core/engine/src/test/kotlin/` package, set
`SOCIETY_DATASET_GOLDEN_DIR` to the Society fixture directory and run the Wardriver
wrapper with `-PvnextCoreOnly :core:engine:test --tests '*SocietyDatasetGoldenTest'`.
The fixture changes because it uses a new ephemeral RSA key and UUIDs. Never
replace these synthetic bytes with a real device key or recording.

The producer's existing `DeviceDatasetWireTest` suite and this generation test
passed on JDK 17/Windows. Node and Chromium-worker tests consume the resulting
exact bytes. This is wire compatibility evidence; it does not establish full
Room admission/projection parity, Android instrumentation or field convergence.
